question: Which of the following is the world's largest basaltic impact crater lake found in India?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Lonar Lake**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Lonar Lake, also known as Lonar Crater, is a saline soda lake located at Lonar in Maharashtra, India.
 
• It is the world's largest basaltic impact crater lake formed by a meteorite impact during the Pleistocene Epoch, approximately 52,000 ± 6,000 years ago.
 
• The lake has a unique ecosystem with both saline and alkaline environments, supporting diverse flora and fauna.
 
• Lonar Lake is a notified National Geo-heritage Monument and attracts scientists, geologists, and tourists from around the world.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Impact Crater:**

 
 
• An impact crater is a circular depression on the surface of a planet, moon, or other celestial body formed by the hypervelocity impact of a smaller body, such as a meteorite.
 
• Impact craters are characterized by a raised rim and, in larger craters, a central peak caused by the rebound of the crust after the impact.
 
 
 
• **Basaltic Rock:**
 
 
• Basalt is a common extrusive igneous rock formed from the rapid cooling of basaltic lava exposed at or very near the surface of a planet or moon.
 
• It is rich in iron and magnesium and low in silica, which gives it a dark color.
 
 
 
• **National Geo-heritage Monument:**
 
 
• National Geo-heritage Monuments are sites that have been identified by the Geological Survey of India (GSI) as being important for geological studies, education, and tourism.
 
• These sites are protected and preserved for their scientific value and natural beauty.
